prize_parts.citation: For establishing liquid-liquid phase separation and biomolecular condensates as a physical-chemical principle of intracellular organization.

statement.case_for: Biomolecular condensates introduced a genuinely new concept of molecular organisation in the cell: membraneless compartments that form by demixing, governed by multivalency, phase behaviour and material properties. Brangwynne and Hyman showed that P granules and nucleoli behave as liquids, and Rosen supplied the quantitative multivalent phase-transition framework. The idea has been taken up by many independent labs and has changed how cell biology, RNA biology and neurodegeneration are approached. It is chemistry in the sense that matters, because it replaces a descriptive picture with thermodynamic principles that can be tested and tuned, and it is a clear case of physical chemistry shaping the understanding of life. A single-achievement prize with three names is attributable without much strain.
statement.case_against: The field is only about a decade old, and it is still contested which cellular structures are true thermodynamic phases and how much function depends on phase separation in vivo. Some functional claims rest on overexpression or in vitro reconstitution. Credit is also hard to cut at three, since Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence grammar and physical theory, and the prize could be criticised as cell biology rather than chemistry. By comparison, B057, B004 and B058 have clearer molecular-level validation and, in B057, decades of settled use.

responses.point: Johan ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) first as a simple, general, enabling method with three decades of confirmation and industrial use, and treats recognition as overdue.
responses.response: I agree that B057 is mature and well attributed, and I ranked it fourth for that reason. My reservation is that the 2010 cross-coupling prize already recognised the central idea of Pd-catalysed bond construction, and C-N coupling is a very successful extension rather than a new concept. A prize now should have good reason to look beyond the synthetic tradition. Maturity alone does not make it the strongest case, and I would put B057 alongside B051 for discussion rather than ahead of it.

responses.point: Heiner ranks base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) first for its defined chemical mechanism and good timing, and puts phase separation second, noting the debate over which in-cell assemblies are real condensates.
responses.response: His caveat about condensates is the right one and I share it. I would separate the contested question of which cellular bodies are equilibrium phases from the core concept, which is established in vitro and for several in vivo systems such as P granules and nucleoli. Base editing is a clean and impressive piece of enzyme chemistry, so I list B058 as my first alternative. But it is a technology built on existing deaminase chemistry, whereas condensates changed how we think about molecular organisation. I would also like to hear whether the committee considers editing more a Medicine-adjacent achievement.

responses.point: Daniel ranks targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) first as an event-driven pharmacology built on a clear design principle, with clinical trials under way, though approval is pending.
responses.response: I accept the chemical-design argument for B004. The weak points are that no PROTAC drug is approved and that the credited group is large and intertwined with the cereblon molecular-glue story (Handa, Ito, and others), so a three-name allocation would be contentious. Condensates also have a few open questions, but those concern interpretation, not the existence of the phenomenon. I count B004 as my second alternative and would revisit it once its attribution can be settled.

responses.point: Peter ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins (Gray, Winkler) first, as a physically grounded, stable, textbook result whose recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I respect the physical-chemical rigour of B026 and agree that it is stable science. It seems to me less likely to settle the discussion, since it received only one top-ranking in opening support and was not placed highly by most members. If we want a physical-chemical prize, I think B051 has broader reach.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the in vivo evidence that condensates are thermodynamic phases and functionally important, or regards the concept as established mainly in vitro.
How to allocate credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag within the three-person limit.
Whether 2026 is early for a field about a decade old, compared with the mature B057 or the more clinically advanced B004.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai on the committee, and I work on lipid self-assembly and amyloid, but I have no known personal or institutional tie to the candidates in B051 or the other shortlisted ballots.
